uncited: It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Direct Illumination with Shadow Rays](2011-direct-illumination-with-shadow-rays.md) by explicitly modeling the hemispheric nature of ambient light through a normal-dependent sky/ground interpolation, and from [Ambient Light Approximation](2244-ambient-light-approximation.md) by using a precomputed occlusion factor derived from ray marching rather than simple geometric heuristics.
- The terrain is represented as a heightfield or voxel grid.
Calculate a bias to offset the shadow ray origin to prevent self-shadowing artifacts on coarse heightfields.
If $NdotL > 0$, trace a shadow ray starting from $\mathbf{p} + \mathbf{n} \times \text{bias}$ with jitter.
Let the result be `shadow` (1.0 if unshadowed, 0.0 if shadowed).
Get the cloud shadow factor: `cloudShade = cloudShadowAt(p.x, p.z, p.y)`.
Compute the ambient occlusion factor by tracing an ambient occlusion ray or hemisphere.
This linearly interpolates between ground-facing ($n_y \approx -1 \Rightarrow \text{sky} \approx 0$) and sky-facing ($n_y \approx 1 \Rightarrow \text{sky} \approx 1$) orientations.
Typical value depends on terrain resolution.
- **Self-Shadowing:** Failing to bias the shadow ray origin results in severe self-shadowing artifacts (acne) on coarse heightfields.
- **Normal Interpolation:** Using finite differences on a bilinear heightfield produces piecewise constant normals, causing visible facet edges.
- **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the shadow ray trace and ambient occlusion trace.
The cost is proportional to the number of samples in each ray.
- **Memory Complexity:** Low, primarily storing the terrain heightfield/voxel data and albedo maps.
- **Strengths:** Provides a visually pleasing approximation of global illumination effects (sky/ground bounce) and shadows with relatively low computational cost compared to full path tracing.
Ambient occlusion is a single-ray approximation.
Cloud shadows are precomputed or approximated.
- **When to use:** Real-time terrain rendering where performance is critical but some indirect lighting and shadowing are desired.
- **When not to use:** When physically accurate soft shadows or complex indirect lighting (e.g., color bleeding) are required.
It is part of a broader effort to create realistic, data-driven terrain visualization using procedural generation and efficient shading techniques.
The approach combines standard direct lighting with a simplified hemispheric ambient model to enhance depth and realism without the cost of full global illumination.
